Springboks at the 2019 Rugby World Cup

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We reveal the magic of the Rugby World Cup and ask whether the Boks can bring the cup home in 2019

Unique Selling Point:
t’s Bokke season! With just days to go, the Rugby World Cup is once again upon us. Since its inception, the Webb Ellis trophy has only ever been won by four countries, and twice by South Africa. Francois Pienaar led the team in the historic ’95 victory and John Smit did it in 2007. Now with a new-look Springbok side, can Siya Kolisi follow in the footsteps of giants and lead the team to victory at the Rugby World Cup?

Summary:
We preview the Springboks participation in the 2019 Rugby World Cup in Japan. We look back on past victories, from the iconic 1995 World Cup held in South Africa to John Smit's 2007 triumph in France. We interview past players, coaches and journalists to provide a definitive retrospective of the Boks at the World Cup. We also interview current players in the squad & attend the squad announcement.

Press Release:


It’s Bokke season! With just days to go, the Rugby World Cup is once again upon us. Since its inception, the Webb Ellis trophy has only ever been won by four countries, and twice by South Africa. Francois Pienaar led the team in the historic ’95 victory and John Smit did it in 2007. Now with a new look Springbok side, can Siya Kolisi follow in the footsteps of giants and become the first black Springbok Captain to win the Rugby World Cup?

Script:


V/O: No other sport epitomises the changing face of South Africa than that of Rugby.

Once regarded as a game that symbolized white oppression, rugby has evolved to become a sport embraced by the majority of South Africans today, who support the Springboks with unmatched patriotic fervour.

That metamorphosis can be traced to a crisp winters day in June 1995, when a beaming Madiba looked on as Francois Pienaar held aloft the William Webb Ellis Trophy, uniting the country like never before

Now 24 years on, can Siya Kolisi’s Springboks win the 2019 Rugby World Cup in Japan and rekindle the spirit of the rainbow nation?



V/O: South Africa was given the honour of hosting the 1995 Rugby World Cup as rugby journalist Dan Retief recalls.

Dan Retief comments

V/O: The ‘95 World Cup provided a stage for new Springbok heroes to emerge, including the black pearl, Chester Williams, the only black player in an all-white squad, who tragically died last Friday from a heart attack.

Dan Retief & Pieter De Villiers on Chester Williams
V/O: Another hero of that team was flyhalf Joel Stransky. His drop goal in the final will never be forgotten

Joel on kicking the winning drop goal

Comments from Dan, Victor, Jean & Joel on the importance of winning the world cup

V/O: 12 years after that famous win, a new generation of Springboks arrived in France for the 2007 Rugby World Cup.

It was a team coached by Jake White and contained some of the best players to ever don the Green & Gold like Captain John Smit, scrumhalf Fourie Du Preez and lock Victor Matfield


Victor on the Boks at RWC 2007

Jean on hoisting Thabo Mbeki into the air

V/O: And so to Rugby World Cup 2019 in Japan. 12 more years have passed since the Boks last won the World Cup and after falling to a lowly 7th in the world rankings 2 years ago, the Boks are back under new coach Rassie Erasmus and South Africa’s first black Captain Siya Kolisi

Comments about the Boks’ renaissance and Siya as a leader

V/O: The team seems to be peaking at the right time. They’re undefeated in 2019 having won the Rugby Championship for the first time, leading to a real sense of optimism when the squad was announced a few weeks ago.


Voxies with some of the Boks following the squad announcement

V/O: As the Boks embark on their World Cup campaign, they know the task ahead of them: They must win 7 games in 7 weeks to become World Champions, starting with an epic encounter against arch rivals and current holders New Zealand next weekend.

Boks v New Zealand

V/O: So does the class of 2019 have what it takes to win the World Cup?

Comments about how to win a rugby world cup.
V/O: Our love affair with the Rugby World Cup began in 1995.

By winning Rugby World Cup 2019, Siya Kolisi’s Boks could bring the country together once more.
